not_done: No model was loaded and no model arm (A, B1, B2, B2@4096, B3) was run; only their command and dry plans were checked. The measurement is the owner's to run on his ThinkPad.
No everyday score harness, no sealed sets, no tests (the owner's rule).

Arms B1 and B2 did not exist in code before this slice; they are built here as the specification and the model-in-loop design (section 9, PROPOSE-2 and NEXT schemas in 6.2) describe them. That is my reading of the specification, not code it already had.
workbench.i05_arms is not added to tools/check_hatch.py's on-demand list (that file is shared; an entry is not required because the module is not named *_checks).
decisions: Conditions arms read the result with joined.result after joined.run; the acceptance checks that result (run_case checks the joined.run observation of today's loop, which holds the result in the adaptive record).

Model turns go through 0.8.7's turns.ask as background kinds with fixed deadlines of 60 s (NEXT) and 120 s (mapping), as the specification set them, because the foreground cap is 20 s and B1 asks more than 3 turns per case. The kinds are registered on first use so that her app's brief priming never picks them up.

'No prompt reuse' in B1/B2/B3: turns are priced as all new and nothing is primed. local_brain still always sends cache_prompt=True, so the server's single slot may reuse a shared prefix; I left local_brain alone and record cache_n per turn so a reader can see it. The README says so.

N asks one question card per stop (listing what it could not read), so 'questions to the owner' counts cards. A clause is read only if phrases from the frozen list cover all of it (joining words aside). That is strict on purpose: a negation or new wording asks the owner and is never taken as a licence.

B3's checker: the decoding, then the pairing unique typed matching settles, then any declaration a phrase licenses. Wording the desk cannot read is left to the model, and the method's own preview still checks it.
Model config defaults are the specification's (context 6144, 4 threads, 4480 MB). B2@4096 always runs at 4096. The kit takes --context, --memory-mb and --backend for the 35B.
Result files record the host only as OS and machine type, never its name.
